colocated-lite-query-timeouts.observation: Repeated four-validator PQ functional runs on one host (four validator processes plus one DHT process) contain unanswered lite-server queries. ExtClient.cpp:69 gives each query a 10.0-second deadline. Three consecutive runs each exposed an observation interval within about one percent of ten seconds. One run recorded node-1 get_masterchain_info=1. A later run recorded total=3 on node-2: get_masterchain_info=2 and lookup_block=1, with one retry inside the interval window. The retry permits a green functional result, so the counters are the only durable indication of the degraded run.

observed_at.cluster_shape: four co-located PQ validators plus one DHT process

colocated-lite-query-timeouts.diagnostic_question: For each timed-out query, did the request reach the selected lite-server? Receipt without a client response localizes the loss to server processing or the response path; no receipt localizes it to ingress or request transport.
colocated-lite-query-timeouts.contract_error_response_fix: run_ext_query now wraps its promise before the first early refusal, serializing any liteServer-contract error as liteServer_error and sending it as an ADNL answer. The generic ADNL query_finished error branch remains silent for non-lite failures; this change does not attribute the previously observed timeouts to the manager path. The source-guard gate checks wrapper ordering and error serialization, including mutations that remove the wrapper or restore set_error.

query_id_trace_follow_up.scope: This exact-commit run identifies one client-side no-transmit timeout. It does not attribute the earlier unjoined timeouts, or rule out admission drops in other runs. One additional query lacked a terminal event when logging ended and was not counted as answered or timed out.

colocated-lite-query-timeouts.no_connection_fail_fast_follow_up: The identified client-side no-transmit branch now returns cancelled/conn not ready before AdnlQuery creation and logs client_refuse with the query id and pending-query count. A disconnected-client behavior test gets the refusal before the transport deadline; the same compiled test then transmits and receives a query on a live connection. The source guard requires the refusal to precede out_queries_.emplace. This fixes the demonstrated branch, but earlier unjoined timeout samples are not attributed by it.
colocated-lite-query-timeouts.closure_condition: The identified no-transmit branch has a fail-fast regression gate. To close the broader observation, join any remaining unanswered query by id through client send, server receipt, server completion and client completion; identify and gate each demonstrated cause. Changing the timeout or relying on retry success is not closure.

colocated-launch-committee-finalcert-tai.observation: A 21-validator, 300-second co-located diagnostic at e586c9dc7 produced 726 agreed masterchain blocks with no lite transport retries. The all-node exposure interval at height 698->699 was 2826.8 ms, while the earliest locally observed Simplex FinalCert timestamps for the matching full block ids were 2751.8 ms apart. This tail is substantially in consensus finalization, unlike other slow exposure intervals that contain material successful-query or local application/exposure time. The run does not identify why this FinalCert interval was long, and co-location remains a caveat rather than a diagnosis. No Simplex, PQ, committee or timeout parameter is changed on this evidence.

observed_at.cluster_shape: 21 PQ validators plus one non-validating verifier and one DHT process on one host

colocated-launch-committee-finalcert-tai.diagnostic_question: What caused the 2751.8 ms interval between first locally observed FinalCert events for agreed blocks 698 and 699: delayed proposals, votes, certificate assembly or another consensus transition, and does that cause occur on one-validator-per-host topology?
colocated-launch-committee-finalcert-tai.closure_condition: Join the full structured Simplex event timeline for this interval to a named consensus transition, reproduce or rule out the cause on a one-validator-per-host topology, and add a regression gate for the demonstrated defect. A long all-node exposure interval alone, preserved agreement or an assumption of co-location is not closure.

colocated-launch-committee-skip-runs.observation: The first five-minute steady-state PQ Simplex observation at the enforced 21-validator launch committee size produced 733 masterchain blocks, from height 13 through 746, in 314 seconds on one co-located host. All 22 queried nodes ended at height 746 and agreed the same full block id at every height 0 through 746, so safety remained intact. This was originally described as cadence p50 399.1 ms against the configured 400 ms target and p95 500.2 ms, with zero lite transport retries. That cadence interpretation is withdrawn: these are all-node agreed-block exposure intervals, ending only when the slowest queried node has applied and exposed the block through its lite-server and answered. They combine consensus finalization, local application, lite-server exposure, query latency and an all-node barrier. Seven exposure intervals lasted 1.3 to 2.3 seconds. The earlier claim that three of those seven were near node2 skip bursts is withdrawn: the text-log count mixed 951 basechain SkipVote lines with 187 masterchain lines, so it correlated different chains. A 180-second committee-wide run at 85be09801 then measured three structured masterchain skip runs (lengths 1, 2 and 3) and five slow exposure intervals; the sets were disjoint. Every slow interval reported coincides_with_skip_run=false, while each skip run occurred in an ordinary interval. Separately, a run at 82f2e8134 contained 576 masterchain SkipVote text lines but no structured skipVote event. The structured channel demonstrably carries skipVote in other runs, so this discrepancy remains open: the text lines may describe relayed peer votes rather than the node's own cast votes, or structured events may have been dropped. Neither reading is established. Co-location is a caveat, not a diagnosis, and this observation is not a reason to tune Simplex or PQ parameters before finalization and exposure are measured separately.

observed_at.cluster_shape: 21 PQ validators plus one non-validating verifier and one DHT process on one host

timing_split_follow_up.tail_assessment: The six intervals are mixed: 698->699 is dominated by a 2751.8 ms first-FinalCert interval; other tails contain shorter FinalCert intervals and material successful-query or local accepted-to-exposed lag. 393->394 has no measured component near its 1200.4 ms all-node observation interval, so it is not attributed to consensus. The per-height and per-node join is in the result artifact and summarized in N6-STATUS-FOR-REVIEW.md. These components are not additive and do not establish a production cause.

text_semantics_follow_up.original_soak3_artifact: LOST_TO_ENVIRONMENT_CLEANUP; the reduced result preserved 576 masterchain text lines and zero structured events, but not the originating text lines or structured batches. The fresh run establishes the source-site semantics and within-horizon invariant; it cannot classify the historical 576 lines individually.

colocated-launch-committee-skip-runs.diagnostic_question: The fresh 21-validator run established that text SkipVote sites have different semantics and that every comparable-window local cast has one structured Voted(skipVote) event. The original soak3's exact 576/0 source lines were lost during environment cleanup and cannot be individually reclassified. The remaining open question is the concrete cause of the slow consensus and non-consensus exposure components on co-located and one-validator-per-host topologies.
colocated-launch-committee-skip-runs.closure_condition: Identify the concrete cause class of the slow intervals on co-located and one-validator-per-host topologies and add a regression gate for each demonstrated defect. The fresh run's classified, node-and-slot-joined local-cast invariant closes the generic text-versus-structured semantics question without pretending to reconstruct the deleted soak3 lines. A raw substring count, an assumption that co-location is responsible, preserved safety, or the now-refuted assertion that skip runs explain the slow intervals is not closure.
